messages:
Grace Kim: can someone point me at the *exact* steps to run the benchmark-lab matrix runner? trying to run H100+A100 sweep for fp8/int8 and i’m not sure what creds i need + where the artifacts end up.

Rina Kobayashi: yep. matrix runner lives in `benchmark-lab` repo (see <https://github.com/benchmark-lab/pull/842|PR #842> if you want context). two ways:
1) local “submitter” that launches jobs to the k8s gpu pools (recommended)
2) fully local (only for microbench, not the full e2e suite)

Isabella Rossi: +1. for the sprint we’ve been doing option (1). high level:
- checkout `benchmark-lab`
- make sure you can auth to the cluster + pull images
- run the runner with a config yaml (models/shapes/workloads/gpu sku)

Grace Kim: ok what auth exactly? i have regular gcloud + kubectl but i keep getting denied when it tries to create jobs

Irene Choi: you need the “benchmark-runner” k8s RBAC role in the perf cluster namespace.
- request is in INT-9923 if you don’t have it yet
- once granted: `gcloud container clusters get-credentials <cluster> --region <region> --project redwood-prod`
- then `kubectl auth can-i create jobs -n benchmark-lab` should return yes

Rina Kobayashi: creds checklist we’ve been using:
- GCP: `gcloud auth login` (or SA if in CI) + cluster creds as Irene said
- Vault: to fetch ephemeral S3/drive creds + internal registry token
  - `export VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.prod.redwood.internal`
  - `vault login` (okta)
- Docker/registry: `gcloud auth configure-docker us-docker.pkg.dev` (if pulling runner images)

Sahana Iyer: also if you’re writing results to the warehouse bucket you need the `bench-artifacts-writer` perm. runner will fail late otherwise.

Grace Kim: where do artifacts go by default? i saw something about drive and also a bucket

Rina Kobayashi: default is:
- raw artifacts (jsonl + stdout/stderr + metadata) -> GCS bucket `gs://redwood-benchmark-artifacts/` under a run id
- summarized aggregates -> uploaded to the shared drive folder if you pass `--drive_upload`
for the fp8/int8 sprint we’ve been uploading *both*.

Isabella Rossi: the shared drive path you’ll see (if drive upload enabled):
`Shared drives/engineering/serving-runtime/benchmarks/fp8-int8/<run_id>/`
Inside you’ll get:
- `results.jsonl`
- `aggregates.csv`
- `env_metadata.json` (git sha, cuda/driver, clocks, model hash)
- optional `nsys/` if you set `--capture_nsys` on selected cases

Grace Kim: nice. do i need google drive creds separately?

Rina Kobayashi: if you run from your laptop, runner uses your corporate oauth via `rwdctl drive login` (one-time). if you run from CI/bot, it uses a drive service account stored in Vault.

BenchmarkLab Bot: Reminder: Drive uploads from local require `rwdctl >= 0.31.4`. Docs: <https://go.redwood.internal/rwdctl/drive>

Grace Kim: ok, what’s the actual command? (sorry 🙏)

Isabella Rossi: typical:
```
git clone git@github.com:redwood/benchmark-lab.git
cd benchmark-lab

# (optional) pin runner image/tag if you’re testing a specific branch
export BENCHLAB_IMAGE_TAG=pr-842

# auth
vault login
rwdctl drive login

auth_kube.sh  # or the gcloud get-credentials command

# run
python3 -m benchlab.matrix_runner \
  --config configs/fp8_int8/h100_a100_top_models.yaml \
  --cluster perf-gpu-us-central1 \
  --namespace benchmark-lab \
  --gcs_prefix gs://redwood-benchmark-artifacts/fp8-int8/ \
  --drive_upload \
  --notes "fp8/int8 sprint run - harness sha + clocks pinned"
```
config defines the matrix: models, prompt dist preset, prefill/decode mix, batch/concurrency, plus gpu sku pools.

Sahana Iyer: if you want clocks pinned (to reduce variance) make sure your config sets:
- `lock_gpu_clocks: true`
- `power_limit_watts: 700` (H100, depends on pool)
that’s from <https://github.com/benchmark-lab/pull/851|PR #851>. without it you’ll see weird p95 drift.

Grace Kim: how do i target specific skus? i need H100 SXM and A100 80GB

Irene Choi: in the yaml there’s a `pools:` section. you want:
- `h100-sxm-80gb` pool (label `gpu.nvidia.com/product=NVIDIA-H100-SXM5-80GB`)
- `a100-80gb` pool
if you use the provided sprint configs they already have the labels. if you roll your own, ping me and i’ll sanity check it.

Rina Kobayashi: also: please don’t point at Dedicated pools. use the perf cluster pools only (we’ve had one collision already this week).

Grace Kim: got it. and where do i see status while it’s running?

Isabella Rossi: runner prints job ids + a dashboard link. quick options:
- `kubectl get jobs -n benchmark-lab -w`
- `kubectl logs job/<jobname> -n benchmark-lab -f`
- Grafana: TTFT/TPOT/tokens/s panels tagged with `run_id` (if you pass `--tag run_id=...`)

Sahana Iyer: if you don’t pass a tag, it autogenerates `run_id` and writes it at the top of output. grab that for debugging.

Grace Kim: last q: what if i need nsys traces for just 3 cases?

Rina Kobayashi: don’t enable globally (huge). add a `profiles:` override block in the config:
- pick cases by model+workload+seq_len bucket
- set `capture_nsys: true` and `nsys_duration_s: 15`
those land under the same GCS prefix in `nsys/` and also get copied to Drive if `--drive_upload` is on.

Grace Kim: perfect. i’ll try now. if i hit RBAC issues i’ll follow up on INT-9923.

Irene Choi: yep. if you’re blocked today, DM me and i can fast-approve.

Isabella Rossi: and please drop your run_id in #eng-runtime when it starts so we don’t duplicate the same matrix :)

Grace Kim: will do, thanks all.
